CRITICAL_CORRECTION_2026_08_15.method_rule: READ THE RECORDS LAYER. datasets/heteronyms/records/*.json are the identity cards, mirrored to the live /who/ surfaces. The .jsonl is an index over them, not the data. Deposits are timestamps; the jsonl is a thin index; the CARDS are the living data.

JD-2_WITHDRAWN.i_asserted: 'Every assigned value is non-canonical. The registry stores Canonical Name (ABBREV) where Press Layer §IV permits the canonical string alone. All 899 values need normalising.'
JD-2_WITHDRAWN.the_truth: MANUS ruling 2026-08-01 EXPLICITLY REVERSED that convention: 'journal field carries the FULL canonical journal name, with the approved abbreviation optionally appended in parentheses — e.g. Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS) — per MANUS ruling 2026-08-01 (reversing the v1.0 abbreviation convention).' The stored values are CORRECT under the governing convention.
JD-2_WITHDRAWN.why_i_got_it_wrong: I read the Press Layer spec (2026-06-11) and treated it as current. A later ruling governed. Same failure as the heteronym cards: an older instrument read as authoritative because I did not look for what superseded it.
JD-2_WITHDRAWN.consequence: 899 values need NO normalisation. A repair I proposed as 'mechanical and safe' would have destroyed a ruled convention.

self_declaration_sweep.searched: all 1,486 titles and descriptions for the eight venue strings
self_declaration_sweep.finding: The signal is far thinner than the raw count suggests. Of 39 apparent self-declarations inside 1-900, only TWO were actual venue declarations for the work in hand (#2 "Written for New Human 2"; #128 "A New Human 2 memographic artifact"), plus the three Semantique Potentielle releases which carry "Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology" in their own titles and which my reading already had right.
why_the_rest_are_not_declarations: CHARTERS name the journal they charter (#516, #651, #838).
MAPS and CALLS name the journals they map or solicit for (#57, #866, #189, #640).
SITE PLANS name the journal whose site they plan (#848).
TOPIC LISTS name a journal among subjects covered (#863).
INSTITUTIONAL packets describe an institution's publication RELATION to a journal, not the packet's own venue (#709, #710).
self_declaration_sweep.substring_bug: 11 of the 63 hits were "New Human 2" matching inside "New Human 2015 Cohort" — the cohort name, not a venue. This is the THIRD substring false positive today, after PER matching inside paper/person/operative in the capture attribution. Word-boundary matching is not optional in this corpus: its vocabulary contains short names that are prefixes of longer ones.
self_declaration_sweep.rule: Self-declaration is CONSIDERED, never definitive, and must be distinguished from mention. The test: does the work say where IT was published, or does it name a journal for some other reason?

archival_findings.title: Operative Semiotics: A Grundrisse — the monograph record is a pointer; the body lives in the planning-documents deposit
archival_findings.detail: Checked at operator request. Recovery IS complete — nothing was lost — but the multi-file Zenodo structure (a book description with several attached files) did not survive as a book. The text landed in #950 "Planning Documents, Algorithms, and Diagnostics" [Working paper], which carries 1,149,275 residual chars. The MONOGRAPH record #1079 "Recovered Edition v1.0" carries only 27,728 and its body_status reads recovery=FULL-AT-DEPOSIT-950 — an explicit pointer away from itself. Hesperus #38 (169,644 chars) is the apparatus; #1343 is a public research edition (RESTORED-20260728); #602 the prosodic algorithm.
archival_findings.consequence: A reader arriving at the monograph finds a stub. The work is whole in the archive and not whole at its own address.
archival_findings.action: Collect #38, #602, #950, #1079, #1343 as one book — Operative Semiotics: A Grundrisse, collected edition — press New Human Press, per operator ruling 2026-08-15. Until then the monograph record should point forward explicitly rather than only in body_status.
